User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user account within the CampusFlow application, encompassing both visitors and administrators. This entity stores core user information required for authentication, role management, and personalized interactions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

email.description: The institutional email address of the user (e.g., @neu.edu.ph), used for login and identification.

role.description: The role of the user within the system, defining their permissions and access levels.

collegeDepartment.description: The college department the user belongs to. Primarily for visitors to specify their affiliation.

isBlocked.description: Indicates if the user account is currently blocked from accessing the application by an administrator.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was initially created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of the last modification to the user account details.

lastLoginAt.description: Timestamp of the user's most recent successful login.

Facility.title: Facility
Facility.description: Represents a physical location or department within the institution where visitors can check in (e.g., Library, Dean's Office).

id.description: Unique identifier for the Facility entity.

name.description: The common name of the facility (e.g., 'Library', 'Dean\'s Office').

description.description: A brief description or additional details about the facility.

Visit.title: Visit
Visit.description: Records details of a single instance of a user visiting a specific facility, including check-in/out times, purpose, and current status.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Visit entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who made the visit. (Relationship: User 1:N Visit)

facilityId.description: Reference to the Facility being visited. (Relationship: Facility 1:N Visit)

checkInTime.description: Timestamp when the user checked into the facility.

checkOutTime.description: Timestamp when the user checked out of the facility. This field is null if the visit is still active.

reasonForVisit.description: The stated purpose or reason for the visit (e.g., 'Inquiry', 'Meeting', 'Research').

status.description: The current status of the visitor within the facility log (e.g., 'Checked-in', 'Waiting', 'In-Meeting', 'Completed').

UserSession.title: UserSession
UserSession.description: Tracks active and past login sessions for users, providing real-time monitoring capabilities for the Admin dashboard.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserSession entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User associated with this session. (Relationship: User 1:N UserSession)

loginTime.description: Timestamp when the user logged in and the session began.

logoutTime.description: Timestamp when the user logged out or the session ended. This field is null if the session is currently active.

isActive.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the user's session is currently active.

firestore.reasoning:
The proposed Firestore structure prioritizes secure, scalable, and debuggable authorization by strictly adhering to the core design principles. The primary strategy revolves around **Authorization Independence via Denormalization** and **Structural Segregation**, ensuring that security rules are straightforward and efficient, avoiding costly `get()` calls.

1.  **Users (`/users/{userId}`):** This collection stores individual user profiles. Access is primarily path-based, where a user can only read or update their own profile (`request.auth.uid == userId`). An administrative role (`roles_admin`) will be granted broader update permissions (e.g., to block users).

2.  **Global Roles (`/roles_admin/{userId}`):** To manage administrative access, a dedicated collection `/roles_admin` is used. The mere **existence** of a document at `/roles_admin/{request.auth.uid}` grants global administrator privileges. This adheres to DBAC, using 'existence over content' and avoiding custom claims or `get()` calls for role verification. Admins have broad read/write access to most collections.

3.  **Facility-Specific Roles (`/roles_facility_manager/{facilityId}/{userId}`):** For staff like Deans or Secretaries who manage specific facilities (e.g., a Dean's Office), this collection provides fine-grained, facility-level authorization. The existence of a document here indicates that `userId` is authorized to manage `facilityId`. This pattern enables rules to check `exists(/roles_facility_manager/$(resource.data.facilityId)/$(request.auth.uid))` without requiring `get()`, maintaining Authorization Independence.

4.  **Facilities (`/facilities/{facilityId}`):** This collection stores static information about institutional facilities. It's generally readable by all authenticated users for lookup purposes but writeable only by global administrators.

5.  **Visits (`/visits/{visitId}`):** This collection records each user's visit to a facility. Crucially, each `Visit` document **denormalizes** `userId` and `facilityId`. This is vital for Authorization Independence and QAPs. Rules can directly compare `request.auth.uid` with `resource.data.userId` for visitor self-management (e.g., checking out) or check `exists(/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid))` or `exists(/roles_facility_manager/$(resource.data.facilityId)/$(request.auth.uid))` for staff/admin access. This enables secure queries (QAPs) for listings like "all visits for this facility today" or "all my past visits" without leaking unauthorized data.

6.  **User Sessions (`/user_sessions/{sessionId}`):** As explicitly requested for the Admin dashboard, this collection tracks active and past user sessions. Each `UserSession` document **denormalizes** `userId` and includes an `isActive` boolean. This denormalization is critical for Authorization Independence: rules can verify `request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId` for users managing their own session (on login/logout) and `exists(/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid))` for admin access. The `isActive` field is key for the real-time Admin dashboard. Administrators can securely query `user_sessions.where('isActive', '==', true)` and receive real-time updates via `onSnapshot`, as the rules will explicitly permit this `list` operation only if `request.auth.uid` corresponds to an admin role. This ensures QAPs are met, as the client's query is fully authorized at the rule level, preventing data leakage.
